**Credit name.** Amund Kristiansen (GitHub @amundsk).

**Claim.** Fourteen new upper bounds at n = 334–504. Each side is the certificate's exact rational side, rounded up at 12 places. In every row the smallest public bound we found is Francisco Couzo's certificate at #763's source commit ([964ee2b](https://github.com/franciscouzo/square-packing/commit/964ee2bdf301d0c8912d956d4010f478dcbbd5ea), `certificates/best/n<N>.cert`); the other public bounds in that repository's comparison files (the register, open issues through #757, Mishapolk/square-packing-records@7e82c64, public Kaggle notebooks through 23 October) are higher, and no registration request since #763 reports these counts (checked 24 October). Kaggle's per-puzzle leaderboard (coordinates not public) shows smaller measured sides at some of these counts; ours are below its figures at 334, 338 and 376.

**Checking.** Both checkers from evand/square-packing at `7982d7a9346e29e36cab3ce075274f3023114353`, exact rational arithmetic, standard library only, accept every certificate: `python3 search/exact/verify_cert.py s<N>_amund.cert` (separating axes) and `python3 search/exact/verify_cert2.py s<N>_amund.cert` (polygon intersection). Figures as printed by `verify_cert.py` (least wall clearance, least pair separation) and `verify_cert2.py` (close pairs), on these exact files; each run takes 1–3 s on a laptop.

A third, unpublished exact check (a local workbench's rational certifier, separate code) also accepted every float packing before certification.

**What the checkers share.** The two public checkers share an author (Evan Daniel) and the certificate format, and the certificates were made with his `dilate_cert.py`; their geometry tests differ. Neither is ours.

**Not done.** No exact KKT solve, rigidity or local-optimality analysis; only the upper bounds are claimed.

**Lineage and credit.** Every packing was found starting from #763's certified packing at the same n, credited as #763 credits it (last column; #763's manifest keeps the earlier seed and construction credits). Matched one-to-one against #763's packing (optimal assignment on centres, best of the eight square symmetries):

| 502 | 0.254 | 8 | 81 | 195 / 200 | Francisco Couzo (square-packing live search); refines the packing of Vladislav Lavrentev (lightningv08), Kaggle "CUDA Packing Search" v11 |

At 372 and 412 no square moves more than 0.1, so by your convention they are refinements of #763's packings; the other twelve are new packings found from them. The searches: for n ≤ 400, 4,096 perturbed variants of the starting packing per round (local melts, re-seated squares, rotated patches), relaxed in a GPU batch (Apple Metal, float32) through a box slightly below the starting side, the best 96 polished in 64-bit with Evan Daniel's `fq` quench, then repeated from the current best for 15–40 rounds; for n > 400, Evan Daniel's `explore.py` (basin explorer with his `fq` quench) for 15–30 min from the starting packing. Credit: Amund Kristiansen, after the packings' credits above; the polish engine, explorer, certificate generator and checkers are Evan Daniel's.

**AI assistance.** Yes. As at #755: the searches, the certificates and this report were done by Claude (Anthropic), working in Claude Code at my direction, using Evan Daniel's open-source engine and checkers and Francisco Couzo's published packings as starting points.
